results.comment: Very good video. Great thurough dive which is always apprecaited.War is always very complicated and I truly hate when people say "he's a mad man" (talking about a leader of country that starts a war) it just drives me crazy. There is always so much more involved in these situations.  6:08 - There's a little more context that needs to be explained about the Warsaw Pact. They weren't exactly satellite states for Russia, they were mostly neutral/free and could reap benefits from NATO and Russia, they did tend to lean towards Russia at the start because they were more economically tied to them.  NATO was formed to counterbalance the Soviet Union and they agreed not to have bordering countries to avoid any potential conflict or escalate tensions. They also both agreed they wouldn't expand. When the Soviet Union dissolved, there was confusion: NATO says: No more Soviet Union so we can expand freely. Russia says: Russia is the Soviet Union and regardless, the Warsaw Pact said you'd never expand.  Lithuania and Estonia joined NATO in 2004 when Russia was just starting to rebound from the economic collapse in the mid-90s (90 was when it started, I think rock bottom was 93/94) But Russia did oppose NATO expansion with these two countries, they just weren't in a position to go to war over them.  8:54 - You keep saying "IF" NATO is hostile. results.comment: This video is very well done and wonderfully informative. However, it does leave out some pretty crucial bits that make this entire conflict seem pretty one-sided.  14:35 - The uprising in 2014 wasn't just some sudden arbitrary occurrence. It was a literal coup of a democratically elected president, instigated by the U.S. and western powers. There's literally a leaked recording of then-U.S. Assistant Secretary of State, Victoria Nuland, weighing in on who Ukraine should put into power after the coup. The coup also involved funding and arming various regimes, one of which was the ultra far-right Social-National Party (a literal neo-nazi party) led by Oleh Tyahnybok and raising them to power to help overthrow the Russian-tolerant government.  22:00 - Russia has not been "fueling a war" in the east. The Donetsk and Luhansk rebellions came about in 2014 after the aforementioned nazis literally caroled Russian-speaking Ukrainians into buildings and set them on fire in Odessa. Donetsk and Luhansk are populated by Russian-Ukrainians (Russian in culture and language). They have been terrorized relentlessly and shelled down on by the aforementioned nazi extremists for 8 years. The vast majority of the 14,000 deaths (22:30) have been on the rebel-held side, 25% of which have been civilians.   22:40 - I'm not sure if it wasn't mentioned because it hadn't just happened yet or not, but in reaction to Russia recognizing Donetsk and Luhansk as independent states (the same way many countries view Isreal or Taiwan as independent states) Germany halted the starting up of the NordStream 2 pipeline (12:12) via an arrangement they'd been strongarmed into signing with the U.S. regarding the lifting of sanctions. This could only be viewed by Russia as a huge act of escalation on the west's part.    There's also no mention of the current U.S. president's son Hunter Biden being given an insanely lucrative $500k salaried position (he had no business having) after the coup, on a Ukraine energy board. There's no mention of NATO's promise to Russia not to move an inch east of Germany, and how they broke that promise again and again and again, 14 different times. There's no mention of the Ukrainian government shutting down 3 Russian news channels as a gift to Biden when he took office, nor is there any mention of the Ukraine president, Zelenski, going to the Munich security conference a week before the invasion and declaring there'd be no more negotiations with the rebels (ending any opportunity of peace) and that Ukraine would possibly pursue nuclear weapons once again--obviously a HUGE threat.  All of these factors seem pretty darn important when understanding the conflict and that while there is a bear terrorizing Ukraine, there's also a lot of people poking that bear.
